relations.evidence: To perform query index operations, the provided user must either be an _Admin_ or assigned the _Query Manage Index_ role. See the [Roles](../../../server/current/learn/security/roles.md#query-manage-index) page for more information.

relations.subject: sdk:collection-management

relations.subject: sdk:bucket-management
relations.evidence: When using a Couchbase version earlier than 6.5, you must create a valid Bucket connection using `Cluster.bucket(name)` before you can use cluster level managers.

relations.subject: n1ql:drop-index
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: structural relation within the page's Index Management section
relations.evidence: To delete a query index you can use the `dropIndex()` or `dropPrimaryIndex()` methods. Which one you use depends on the type of query index you wish to drop from the database.

cross_product_finding: This is the batch's clearest example favoring STATEMENT reuse over minting an SDK-specific duplicate: the page's own text equates the SDK's QueryIndexManager operations with the underlying N1QL statements ('managing indexes used for queries'), names the exact privilege label from the registry ('Query Manage Index'), and links directly to server/'s Roles page anchor for it. Unlike sqlpp-queries-with-sdk.json (a generic ad-hoc query, correctly SDK-specific) or full-text-searching-with-sdk.json (no SQL++ equivalent at all, necessarily SDK-specific), this page is fundamentally ABOUT running CREATE INDEX/CREATE PRIMARY INDEX/DROP INDEX/DROP PRIMARY INDEX/BUILD INDEX through a typed Java API, so I reused n1ql:create-index, n1ql:drop-index, and n1ql:build-index directly as the subjects/objects rather than minting sdk:query-index-manager. SECOND FINDING: this page explicitly disclaims any connection to Capella's management plane - 'This part of the SDK API predates the Capella Management API, and is only intended to work with self-managed Couchbase Server clusters. Management of your Capella Operational cluster is available away from the Web UI with the Capella Management API' - so requiresCapellaRole is explicitly NOT applicable to BucketManager/CollectionManager/QueryIndexManager; Capella cluster provisioning goes through a wholly separate API surface outside this page's scope. Combined with the finding on sdk-user-management-example.json, neither of the two pages the coordinator flagged as requiresCapellaRole candidates actually uses that mechanism - both are firmly on the self-managed-cluster/data-plane side of the fence.
